tasks.name: HumanoidBench level-ground walk
tasks.description: Walk forward on level ground under the source 1000-step episode and meet its episode-return success line.
tasks.source_task_or_operation: HumanoidBench walk: sustain forward locomotion near the source 1 m/s walking regime without falling.
tasks.applicability: The canonical Unitree G1 is a free-base biped with two six-joint legs, foot sites, IMU observations, and 29 position-controlled hinges. Level-ground walking uses those leg and base degrees of freedom and does not require articulated fingers. This establishes physical applicability only, not achieved performance.
tasks.adaptation: Adapt the benchmark operation to canonical G1 while retaining the source 1000-control-step horizon, per-step reward formula, and success_bar 700. Rebind source body and sensor semantics. The pinned repository's auxiliary G1 adaptation has 37 task actuators, including fourteen articulated-hand motors, and is not the canonical model; this exact package has 29 actuators, including six differing waist/wrist channels and no articulated hands. Compute force tolerances for all 29 canonical actuators, append eight zero tolerance entries, and take the source-sized 37-term mean. This preserves the source denominator, penalizes every canonical actuator, and cannot gain control reward from the actuator-count reduction. The canonical position-actuator interface remains unchanged.
scene_assumptions: A level rigid floor provides unobstructed travel along the requested world-frame direction for the full source horizon.
observation_assumptions: The evaluator samples canonical free-base state, joint state, foot contacts, IMU orientation, actuator force, and simulation time from MuJoCo.
Episode return is recomputed from the pinned source formula after the recorded canonical-name and 37-term force-mean substitutions.

source_refs.specific_reference: envs/basic_locomotion_envs.py lines 16-18 and 21-102: Walk uses 1 m/s, success_bar=700, the repository's auxiliary G1 branch sets stand height to 1.28 m, and the code defines standing/upright/control/move reward; tasks.py sets 1000 steps. Paper Section IV-A names walk as a distinct 1 m/s task and Figure 3 defines episode return as the reward sum.
source_refs.adaptation: Keep 700 and 1000 steps. Rebind state names; average all 29 canonical actuator-force tolerances with eight zero padding entries, preserving the source 37-term denominator and preventing an actuator-count reward increase.

tasks.name: RoboCup high kick
tasks.description: Kick a stationary ball from the ground into the goal at or above a declared minimum crossing height.
tasks.source_task_or_operation: RoboCup Humanoid League High-Kick Challenge.
tasks.applicability: The canonical G1 has independently actuated legs and feet and a free base, making a height-directed stationary-ball kick physically applicable. The task uses no hands. This task record does not assert that the goal can be scored.
tasks.adaptation: The canonical 1.219 m stand model selects the source AdultSize field and FIFA size 5 ball. Preserve the declaration rule: minimum height is at least two thirds ball diameter and a 0.01 m increment, initial robot distance is at least 0.3 m, and only a goal crossing at or above the declaration counts. Preserve the 25 minute limit.

tasks.name: RoboCup collision-free obstacle navigation
tasks.description: Cross the AdultSize field strip without touching or knocking over any of five obstacles and without leaving the strip.
tasks.source_task_or_operation: RoboCup Humanoid League Obstacle Navigation Challenge.
tasks.applicability: The 1.219 m canonical G1 falls in the source AdultSize height class and is a steerable free-base biped with collision and base-state observations. Navigating around full-height obstacles is physically applicable and independent of hand articulation. No crossing result is claimed.
tasks.adaptation: Select source AdultSize values unchanged: 3 m strip width across the 9 m field width, five obstacles, each 1 m high and 0.6 m wide, and randomized legal placement. Preserve full success as reaching the opposite sideline with no obstacle contact and no partial or full strip exit.
scene_assumptions: A 3 m-wide by approximately 9 m-long AdultSize field strip contains five rigid colored obstacles, each 1 m high and 0.6 m wide. Candidate centers form the source 3 by 3 grid at one-quarter increments of strip width and length; no more than two obstacles share a longitudinal row, and outer placements leave less than canonical robot width to the boundary so a passable interior route remains.
observation_assumptions: The evaluator samples canonical base and body poses, obstacle and boundary contacts, strip-boundary crossing, opposite-sideline contact, and time.

source_refs.specific_reference: Section_III/obstacle_navigation.tex lines 15-28 and 31-66: AdultSize strip width is 3 m; five obstacles are 1 m high and 0.6 m wide; nine candidate locations use quarter-width and quarter-length increments with a passable route; success reaches the opposite sideline without obstacle contact or partial/full strip exit. law1.tex lines 98-103 fixes the approximately 9 m AdultSize field width; general-rules.tex supplies the 25 minute limit.

tasks.name: RoboCup long stride
tasks.description: Step both feet completely across a declared ground gap without either foot touching the center line, gap interior, or far string.
tasks.source_task_or_operation: RoboCup Humanoid League Long Stride Challenge.
tasks.applicability: The canonical G1 has articulated legs, two named feet, and sufficient free-base motion to take a measured stride. The operation is entirely leg-based and physically applicable without finger joints. This does not assert any particular attainable gap distance.
tasks.adaptation: Represent the center line and string as contact-observable narrow fixtures. Preserve the source full-success definition that both feet finish beyond the string without touching either boundary or the intervening region, the best-run aggregation, and the 25 minute limit. The requested gap is not claimed reachable in advance.

source_refs.adaptation: Use MuJoCo contact and foot-position predicates for the same source boundaries and both-feet completion. Preserve best-run and time rules; leave gap distance as a declared task parameter rather than inventing a pass distance.
